The framework models legal risk as a function of source integrity (S), where S ∈ [0,1]. A Bayesian update on S yields posterior risk estimates. Security design is modeled as a ternary system (D, C, S), where D represents deployment complexity, C cost efficiency, and S secret exposure. When D > 0.8, system vulnerability increases exponentially. Demo readiness is evaluated through V (value clarity), F (fixture quality), and P (story alignment). These variables form a triadic vector space where V < 0.4 implies delayed partner outreach. Each primitive operates under distinct breakdown regimes, yet all converge into a unified adversarial risk landscape. Failure modes include unchecked legal claims, insecure deployments, and unvalidated demos—each mapped to a probabilistic risk kernel within GSI’s Bayesian inference framework and GSE’s state-transition engine.
